name: hz_r1_ladder_v1
decision: Does the native family's loss-versus-training-compute frontier keep improving with a stable or rising exponent from 1e16 to 1e18 FLOPs, does depth keep paying as compute grows, and where do the flagship and the memory-only member (cheapest on event hardware) diverge? Selected compute-optimal arms are scored once on the sealed public protocol and placed against the published modded-NanoGPT curves.
public_scoring: after the ladder: one sealed public-protocol score per variant and budget for the compute-optimal arm only (--mode public)

worker.note: GPU worker guards for run_safe.sh: CUDA reserves far more virtual address space than it uses, so the virtual cap is unlimited; the whole-job RSS watchdog, host MemAvailable floor and exact checkpoints stay. Set rss_cap_kb to >= 3x the largest RSS seen in the plan phase.

declaration: Stationarity/online: fixed-weight language protocol on a stationary corpus; one pass over fresh lanes, so each update's pre-update loss is a held-out prequential loss. Online weight adaptation is not part of this compute-frontier comparison (the published curves are fixed-weight); it is scored separately on PTB/WikiText-2.

Fighter rationale: plan-B deep keyed temporal-memory member, the composition where depth pays on CPU (one pass 4M: L8 5.8414 vs L2 5.8648, gap growing with data); executed by exact GPU kernels (contract: loss and every gradient equal DeepKeyedLM to 3e-6, curie_gpu_ladder_contract_20261016_v1). memory_only drops the per-layer reads (O(1) state per step, the cheapest member on event hardware) to test whether persistent memory alone carries the scaling.
State/history: persistent temporal memory and keyed reads over each 1024-token lane with full backprop over the lane; evaluation in 1024-token windows (the public protocol's windows).

Retained: decaying/rotating temporal memory, sparse token-slot keyed writes (output bonus), separate keys/values, race-attention reads per layer (flagship). Not included: hard routes and counterfactual route credit (full-backprop member), asynchronous event timing (unit steps on token streams).
Restrictions: none imposed for symmetry; bf16 matmuls with fp32 memory kernel, attention and loss (execution precision).
Resources: measured FLOPs/token and tokens/s per shape in the plan phase; one training process on the GPU; exact resume every --checkpoint-every steps and on SIGTERM.
